question: What is Morgan Stanley's strategy to increase their net new assets?

claims.text: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Ted Pick stated that Morgan Stanley continues to invest in each of its three business segments 'via human capital and technology,' and that growth plans embed 'the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya attributed Morgan Stanley's record results to 'the execution of our strategy, particularly our sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel' which 'allowed us to reach more clients and deepen existing relationships,' citing financial advisers, a culture of innovation, unique capabilities and products as 'the foundation of our business.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said net new assets of $232 billion 'reflect the strength of our core business and the differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm,' noting that 'our pipeline and our connectivity across channels allows us to build relationships early and deepen them over time.'
In the 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19), Morgan Stanley attributes the level of net new assets in a given period partly to 'our ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Ted Pick described the wealth business as 'built for scale and performance,' stating the advisor, workplace and E*TRADE retail channels 'are each thriving' and that 'the funnel is working.'

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley continues 'investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel' that 'serve as an engine for future growth.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Ted Pick credited Morgan Stanley's position to 'the integrated scaling of the funnel,' citing a self-directed channel that 'continues to innovate for clients,' a differentiated workplace offering 'that continues to expand and source new relationships,' and 'deep trust-based relationships between the financial advisers and their clients.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Ted Pick noted that Morgan Stanley 'translated institutional strength into client value through our adviser-led and E*TRADE channels,' as Wealth Management added a record $148 billion in organic net new assets driven by large IPOs of late-stage private workplace clients.
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), Ted Pick stated that 'investments in our self-directed and Workplace channels drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel.'

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said advisor-led flows were 'originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Morgan Stanley reported that 'Advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships accelerated, growing to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared to historical averages of around $60 billion per year.'

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya credited the quarter's net new assets to 'broad-based strength across channels, inclusive of elevated flows related to advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting events, positive recruiting trends, and self-directed clients.'

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), Ted Pick described the advisor value proposition at 'the top of the funnel' as offering 'unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating,' with 'a lot of inbound inquiry' from advisors expected to continue.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the advisor-led channel was 'attracting assets held away' and 'bringing in new clients, and that's a lot of the tools that we've been giving to our advisors.'

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said channel migration of workplace assets toward advice 'has helped to contribute to over $1 trillion of total assets in our adviser-led strategy.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley generated '$1 trillion of net new assets in the 3 years subsequent to the acquisition of E*TRADE' and, per the transcript, 'another $1 trillion' over the last 3 years, describing 'reinvestment from within the funnel.'
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the advisor-led channel drove 2024 results 'from new clients and existing clients, new clients being really important.'
On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said '70% of the flows that come from workplace... is actually net new assets to the firm.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said 'Assets that originated from workplace continue to migrate into our advisor-led channel as a result of the consistent investments we have made into our differentiated platform.'
On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya characterized the workplace channel as 'a powerful asset acquisition tool,' with the reopening of the IPO market supporting results.
On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley has 'about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in terms of our workplace pipeline.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Ted Pick said the 'Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said fee-based flows included 'a new corporate retirement mandate' and, per the 3Q26 press release, fee-based flows of $80 billion 'included a new corporate retirement mandate.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya cited 'investing, deepening our competitive moats in areas like our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley is 'working on that referral model' for workplace clients without an advice-based relationship, which 'can begin as early as the financial education spot' and includes '401(k)s and new 401(k) assets.'
On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said 'we saw greater asset retention from Workplace, which translated into NNA' as vesting occurred.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said self-directed channel 'year-over-year improvement... comes from investments in marketing and business development' and cited 'new tools like E*TRADE Pro.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Ted Pick said there is 'continued work that we're doing in E*TRADE to take a world-class platform and continue to make that interesting for our active self-directed community.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), a company representative said Morgan Stanley has 'been investing in that business in the E*TRADE franchise, in E*TRADE Pro,' while also using technology 'both on the cost and the revenue side,' including AI on the revenue side.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya cited 'LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.'
On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley has 'been increasing our marketing and business development' in self-directed.

In the 2025 10-K, Morgan Stanley describes its Wealth Management competitive position as affected by factors including 'our brand and reputation, the breadth, depth and pricing of our product offerings and our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.'

adjacent.text: On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya cited positive advisor recruiting trends as one contributor to net new assets; the 10-K also cites 'our ability to attract and retain financial advisors' as a driver of NNA.
adjacent.differs_because: These are qualitative references to recruiting and retention as drivers of NNA; neither firm discloses advisor headcount additions, departures or attrition on a comparable basis.

adjacent.text: The 2026 Morgan Stanley Retirement Plan Survey, conducted July-August 2026 by 8 Acre Perspective with 200 sponsors, found 34% of plan sponsors believe the DC plan is employees' most valued benefit, up from 15% in 2024.
adjacent.differs_because: This is an independent survey of plan sponsor perceptions of retirement benefits, not Morgan Stanley's stated strategy for gathering retirement assets into wealth management.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not disclose a quantitative advisor recruitment target, retention rate, or headcount attrition figures; only qualitative references to 'positive recruiting trends' and the ability to 'attract and retain financial advisors' appear in the evidence.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley financial supplement advisor headcount / retention disclosures or recruitment announcements.

gaps.what: Specific retirement plan (401(k)/DC) asset-gathering metrics, such as retirement plan assets or participant flows into wealth management, are not disclosed in the evidence provided; the evidence covers workplace stock plan metrics and a corporate retirement mandate mention but not a dedicated retirement channel asset figure.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Workplace/retirement channel disclosures, such as retirement plan assets or participant counts by plan type.

gaps.what: Detailed self-directed digital product roadmap and specific E*TRADE growth initiatives beyond E*TRADE Pro, marketing/business development spend, and AI tools (LeadIQ) are not fully disclosed in the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley self-directed/digital channel disclosures or product announcements with E*TRADE feature specifics.
